evidence.quote: There is a curious thing about races, if you have ever noticed it, monsieur. To a Frenchman or an Englishman two, shall we say, Japanese women will look pretty much alike; but if there exists a real likeness between two eastern women, even though it is not very strong to their fellows, a Westerner will be unable to distinguish between them
evidence.paraphrase: The narrator's source offers a generalization about how Westerners perceive resemblance between eastern women, framing the twins' indistinguishability.

evidence.quote: A burly prison warden in white with a huge revolver at his hip came in for tobacco, and she found herself thinking, "Good heavens, that thing is a man!" She was contrasting him with Carstairs.
evidence.paraphrase: Cerise reacts to the aftermath of the kiss by mentally contrasting other men unfavorably with Carstairs.

evidence.quote: He didn\u2019t kiss you, he kissed Marianne. He had mistaken her for Marianne; the warmth about her heart belonged to Marianne
evidence.paraphrase: Cerise realizes the kiss was given to her in mistaken identity for her twin sister.

evidence.quote: how she had asked him to meet her in the name of Marianne, knowing that in the dark, in the moonlight, he would not know the difference between them
evidence.paraphrase: Cerise exploited the twins' indistinguishable likeness to impersonate her sister at a moonlit meeting.

evidence.quote: Monsieur Carstairs, who was responsible for the death of Cerise, had, to his own knowledge, never even seen the girl. He had heard Marianne speak of her sister, but as they were never in the shop together he did not know of the extraordinary likeness.
evidence.paraphrase: The story's resolution turns on the fact that Carstairs caused a woman's death without ever knowingly meeting her, owing to the twins' likeness.

evidence.quote: To this day, if he is alive, Monsieur Carstairs does not know that he is responsible for a woman\u2019s death. He will not know till the judgment comes; and that is a thought to give one pause, for does any man know his full account or the consequences of his sins?
evidence.paraphrase: Roche reflects on the unknowable full consequences of a person's actions and sins.

evidence.quote: she turned as if to pick up some trifle and, turning again, drove the knife into his throat.
evidence.paraphrase: Marianne fatally stabs Carstairs with a cane knife when he returns to the shop.
